subject: ophthalmology
title: Lens and cataract

steps.tx: **Senile cataract** clouds with age by type: cortical (spoke opacities, glare, monocular polyopia), nuclear (brunescent browning with myopic shift improving near vision, second sight), posterior subcapsular (central plaque glaring in bright light, diabetics and steroid users), and hypermature Morgagnian (liquefied cortex with sinking nucleus, phacolytic glaucoma risk). Symptoms are painless blurring, glare, halos, frequent glass changes and fading colours. Maturation runs immature to mature to hypermature; intumescent lenses swell shutting angles.
steps.say: Glare plus frequent glass changes in elderly is cataract. Browning nucleus brings second sight before blindness.

steps.tx: **Congenital cataract** blinds amblyopically if missed: leukocoria with absent red reflex in newborn screening, unilateral (persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous, trauma) or bilateral (rubella with salt and pepper retinopathy and deafness, galactosaemia with oil drop cataract reversible by diet, Down syndrome, hypocalcaemia). Dense bilateral disease operates within weeks (lensectomy with vitrectomy in infants, IOL after age two debates), unilateral within days, followed by aggressive amblyopia patching and refraction. Rubella vaccination and galactose restriction prevent selected cases.
steps.say: White pupil in newborn is cataract until screened: operate dense bilateral within weeks. Rubella triad adds deafness and retinopathy.

steps.tx: Modern surgery is **phacoemulsification** with foldable intraocular lens: topical anaesthesia, small clear corneal incision, capsulorhexis, ultrasound sculpting with irrigation aspiration, in the bag IOL targeting emmetropia by biometry. Extracapsular extraction suits hard brown nuclei; intracapsular (cryo) belongs to subluxated lenses. IOL power formulas (SRK patterns) need axial length and keratometry; astigmatism managed by toric lenses or limbal relaxing incisions. Same day bilateral surgery stays selective for risk.
steps.say: Phaco with in bag lens through a small wound is the modern standard. Biometry picks lens power.

steps.tx: **Posterior capsular opacification (after cataract)** hazes months later (Elschnig pearls, fibrous membrane) and opens with Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy, not repeat surgery. Operative risks include posterior capsular rupture with vitreous loss, dropped nucleus, iris trauma, endophthalmitis (see uveitis wave), cystoid macular oedema (Irvine Gass), retinal detachment in myopes, and refractive surprise. Phacomorphic (swollen lens closing angle) and phacolytic (leaked protein clogging trabeculum with hypermature) glaucomas complicate neglected cataracts urgently.
steps.say: Blur months after good cataract surgery is after cataract: YAG it open. Swollen white lens with high pressure is phacomorphic.
